theme: 13F holdings parsers and institutional-ownership history, short-interest datasets, insider-transaction parsers (Form 4), ETF holdings trackers

candidates.name: talsan/ishares
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package that scrapes iShares.com daily ETF holdings-history CSVs (per-fund, per-date constituent weights/shares) for every iShares fund, with optional AWS S3 + Athena integration for building a historical archive; README + README_Quant.md document the pull format. Not a static dataset itself but a repeatable one-command method to build a point-in-time ETF-holdings-history table (would need ABNB tickers e.g. IWF, IJR-style large/mid growth funds filtered post-run).
candidates.why_useful: Could be run to build a genuine point-in-time series of ABNB's weight/shares inside iShares ETFs over time (institutional-ownership proxy, gap 15), which is otherwise only in licensed 13F/consensus data; also useful for peer OTAs/hotel ETF weight tracking.
candidates.time_coverage: daily snapshots from whenever run against iShares.com; no long history bundled in repo (must be run repeatedly to accrue vintages)
candidates.size_hint: code repo only (~6.6KB README); output size depends on run duration

candidates.name: evdubs/spdr-etf-holdings
candidates.what_it_holds: Shell/ETL scripts (extract-transform-load.sh) that download and parse SPDR (State Street) ETF holdings XLS documents into structured form; MPL-2.0 licensed, README ~2.6KB describing the pipeline. No committed historical data, just the puller.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as the iShares tool above but for SPDR funds (XLY consumer discretionary, sector ETFs that hold ABNB) — a repeatable way to snapshot ABNB's ETF-holding weight/shares if run on a schedule, feeding an institutional-ownership-concentration proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: point of run only, no bundled history

candidates.name: kovagent/shortkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Rust crate/tool bundling US short-sale volume and FINRA short-interest data as parquet files, with a nightly-refresh mechanism and no API keys required (per description). Repo is small (has CHANGELOG.md, .github workflow) so likely thin, but the described data product is exactly FINRA short interest by ticker over time.
candidates.why_useful: If the bundled parquet actually carries multi-year FINRA short-interest history for ABNB and comparable tickers, it would give a free, non-licensed, point-in-time-able short-interest series to complement the options/short-interest data we already hold in-house (check whether it's finer-grained/free vs. what we already pay for).
candidates.time_coverage: nightly refresh going forward; historical depth unclear without deeper inspection
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partially duplicates existing short-interest data already held, but may be free/finer-grained/more current

candidates.name: efebiskin/sec-form4-parser
candidates.what_it_holds: Pip-installable, dependency-free, typed Python parser for SEC Form 4 insider-trading XML filings (converts EDGAR Form 4 XML into structured transaction records: insider name, role, transaction date, shares, price). No data bundled — a parsing library only, to be pointed at EDGAR full-text/XBRL Form 4 filings.
candidates.why_useful: A clean building block for constructing an ABNB insider-transaction history (Form 4s already public on EDGAR) without hand-rolling XML parsing; could feed an insider-buying/selling signal panel alongside the existing guidance ledger.
candidates.time_coverage: method only; covers whatever EDGAR range is queried (EDGAR Form 4 history back to ~1996 in XML from ~2003)

candidates.name: lucabol/FollowTheGuru
candidates.what_it_holds: 13F parsing and visualization tool for investor portfolios identified by CIK (pulls EDGAR 13F-HR filings, parses XML holdings tables, visualizes by manager). Very low activity (1 star, last updated 2021), no bundled dataset.
candidates.why_useful: A minimal reference implementation for parsing 13F-HR XML by CIK; could be adapted to build an institutional-ownership-concentration time series for ABNB (gap 15) but would need real rework given its age/inactivity.
candidates.time_coverage: method only, whatever EDGAR range queried (13F-HR filings since ABNB's 4Q20 IPO quarter onward)

candidates.name: mileshenrichs/openholdings
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 Python package to "retrieve full ETF holdings lists with a single Python function" — a thin client presumably wrapping fund-provider holdings pages/APIs into one call. No bundled data.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction alternative to the iShares/SPDR-specific scrapers above if it covers multiple fund families in one interface; would need inspection to confirm ABNB-holding ETFs (consumer discretionary, travel, growth funds) are covered.
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time pulls only, no history bundled

candidates.name: Finnhub-Stock-API/finnhub-python
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python client (1074 stars, Apache-2.0) for the Finnhub API, which offers (per free tier, rate-limited) institutional ownership, insider transactions, ETF holdings/country/sector exposure, and short-interest-adjacent fundamentals endpoints alongside real-time price data. No data committed — a general API client; usefulness is gated on Finnhub's free-tier limits for these specific endpoints (untested here).
candidates.why_useful: One client could in principle pull ABNB institutional-ownership history, insider transactions, and ETF-holdings country/sector breakdowns without separately licensed data, if the free tier actually exposes historical (not just current) values — worth a human check of Finnhub's free-tier scope before relying on it.
candidates.time_coverage: depends on Finnhub API entitlement, unconfirmed

candidates.name: bdi2357/iShares_ETF_holdings_downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed script for downloading iShares ETF holdings (simpler alternative to talsan/ishares, no AWS integration, 3 stars).
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight fallback method to the more complete talsan/ishares tool for the same purpose (pulling ABNB's weight in iShares consumer/growth funds).

candidates.name: tarikceric/Price-Trends-for-ARK-investments
candidates.what_it_holds: Tracks ARKK/ARKX (Cathie Wood ARK Invest) daily holdings-disclosure files (ARK publishes daily CSV holdings) with analysis in pandas and export to PostgreSQL. ARK's own daily-published CSVs are a genuine free historical daily-holdings source going back to ARK fund inception (~2014) if the repo or ARK's site is used directly.
candidates.why_useful: ARK funds are known to have held/traded growth-consumer names; a working daily-ARK-holdings puller/archiver is a real historical-frequency institutional-ownership proxy source (higher frequency than 13F) for whichever names it covers, worth checking if ABNB ever appeared in ARKK/ARKX baskets.
candidates.time_coverage: method only; ARK publishes daily CSVs historically back to fund inception if pulled/archived

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: no repo surfaced with a large committed historical dataset of 13F holdings, Form 4 transactions, or short interest specifically for ABNB or even generically at scale — everything found is a PARSER/CLIENT (method), not a stored dataset, confirming CONTEXT.md's framing that gap 15 (13F concentration history) is a genuine hole. The strongest finds are the two ETF-holdings scrapers (talsan/ishares with AWS/Athena integration, and the SPDR ETL) which could be RUN going forward to start accruing a point-in-time ETF-weight series for ABNB, and Finnhub's official Python client which may expose institutional-ownership/insider-transaction endpoints on its free tier (unconfirmed, needs human check of quota/entitlements — do not assume it's free of a paid-key requirement given the project rule against paid API keys). No repo held a pre-scraped/archived dump of WhaleWisdom-style 13F aggregation, no FINRA short-interest historical CSV dump beyond the small kovagent/shortkit project (recent, unverified depth), and no dedicated Form-4-history-for-a-ticker dataset. Two `gh search repos` calls with combined quoted terms returned zero results because gh ANDs multiple quoted args together rather than OR-ing them — worth noting for future scouts on this modality. Recommend a future pass try `gh search code` sparingly for "CIK 0001559720" (ABNB's own EDGAR CIK) to find any repo that already committed ABNB-specific 13F/Form-4 pulls, which plain repo search did not surface.
